Performers
The U.S. Army Strings (string orchestra) Documented

Commons credits the artist as “Orchestra d’archi dell’esercito degli Stati Uniti”; the archived Army Band download page is headed The U.S. Army Band “Pershing’s Own” – Army Strings Audio Downloads. Neither names a conductor or soloist. IMSLP lists a 14:53 recording from the U.S. Army Band (uploaded 2010) with the U.S. Army Strings under Lt. Col. John Clanton; the Commons page does not confirm that it is the same file.

[1] [2]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The Commons description says only “Fantasia su un tema di Thomas Tallis”. Which of the 1910, 1913 and 1919 versions is played, the performing edition and the number of players in each group are not stated.

[1] [2]
Recorded
Unknown Unknown

Commons gives “circa 2010” for the file. That is the uploader’s date for the recording, not a documented session date.

[1]
Place
Unknown Unknown

The ensemble’s home base does not establish the recording venue.

Unknown Unknown

The file came from the U.S. Army Band’s own download page, not from a commercial label.

Catalogue
Unknown Unknown

No catalogue number is supplied.

Matrix, take, sides
Unknown Unknown

No matrix, take or original carrier is identified; the digital file alone does not settle whether such identifiers exist.

[1]
Transfer
Imported to Wikimedia Commons from Italian Wikipedia (FileImporter); original source: the U.S. Army Band download page. Documented

The Commons import comment and the Credit field give this chain. No personal mastering credit is stated.

[1] [2]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The Commons file timestamp (4 October 2012) is an import date, not a transfer or session date.

[1]
Processing
Ogg Vorbis file with an MP3 access derivative supplied by Wikimedia Commons. Documented

Earlier processing by the Army Band (its page offered MP3 files compressed in zip format) is not documented.

[1]
Composition rights
Vaughan Williams’s copyright in the music runs to the end of 2028 in the UK and EU; the Fantasia (first published 1921) is in the public domain in the United States and Canada. Documented

The Vaughan Williams Foundation gives 2028 as the year copyright in his music expires; IMSLP records the work as public domain in Canada and the United States and not in countries with life plus 70 years. Any modern edition has its own rights.

[4] [3]
Recording rights
Public domain, as declared on the Wikimedia Commons file page. Inferred, not documented

The licence status is declared on the file page, but the template used there ({{PD-Old}}) concerns the age of the composition, which cannot apply to Vaughan Williams’s music in the UK or EU, and says nothing about the recording. The likely basis is that a U.S. Army Band recording is a work of the U.S. government; neither the file page nor the archived Army Band page says so. IMSLP lists the 14:53 Army Strings recording under Creative Commons Attribution 3.0.

[1] [2]

Ralph Vaughan Williams, Fantasia on a Theme by Thomas Tallis; The U.S. Army Strings, U.S. Army Band “Pershing’s Own”. Public domain as declared on Wikimedia Commons; original source the Army Band’s download page. Vaughan Williams’s copyright subsists in the UK and EU until the end of 2028.
